config.footerNote: Questions are original practice items written to match the official AQA GCSE French (8652) specification themes and paper structure. This app has no audio, so Listening items are presented as written transcripts for reading practice, not exam-realistic listening simulation. Model answers are indicative exemplars only, not official AQA mark schemes.

Paper 1.Listen and answer: AO1 (Listening): marks are awarded for accurate, relevant comprehension of the spoken/written French. Partial credit is given for identifying the correct detail even if the English expression is imperfect; answers must match what is stated, not inferred beyond the text.

Paper 2.Describe the photo: AO2 (Speaking): assessed on communication of relevant content, range and accuracy of language, and pronunciation/intonation. Higher marks require description plus opinion plus justification, not description alone.
Paper 2.Role-play: AO2 (Speaking): assessed on task completion (all bullet points covered), appropriateness of response, and ability to deal with an unpredictable question. Accuracy and spontaneity are credited over complexity.

Paper 3.Reading comprehension: AO3 (Reading): marks for accurate extraction of explicit and implicit meaning from the French text; answers must be supported by the text and expressed clearly in English.
Paper 3.Translate into English: AO3 (Reading)/translation: marked for accuracy of meaning first, then grammatical accuracy of the English produced; omissions and mistranslations of tense/negatives lose marks.

Paper 4.Translate into French: AO4 (Writing)/translation: marked on accuracy of meaning and of French grammar (verb endings, agreement, word order); partial credit is given per correctly translated sense unit.
Paper 4.Write in French: AO4 (Writing): assessed on content (covering all bullet points), range of vocabulary/structures, accuracy, and quality of opinions with justification. Using a range of tenses accurately accesses higher marks.
